title: Arithmetic & Other Operators
summary: + - * / // % ^ for math, .. to concatenate strings, # for lengths, plus compound assignments like +=. A complete operator cheat sheet.

details.heading: Arithmetic
details.body: `+ - * /` standard math · `//` floor division · `%` modulo (remainder) · `^` power (right-associative, float result) · unary `-`.

details.heading: Strings & lengths
details.body: `..` concatenates strings (converts numbers automatically). `#s` is a string's length; `#t` a table's array length.

details.heading: Precedence highlights
details.body: `^` binds tightest, then unary ops, then `* / // %`, then `+ -`, then `..`, comparisons, `and`, `or`. Use parentheses when in doubt: `-2^2 == -4`, but `(-2)^2 == 4`.

explanation.whatItIs: The symbols that compute: math operators, string glue (`..`), the length probe (`#`), and shorthand updaters (`+=`).
explanation.whyItExists: Every game tick does arithmetic — damage, timers, economy. Short forms keep it compact.
whenToUse: `//` when you need whole chunks: `seconds // 60` = minutes
whenNotToUse: `..` in hot loops — use table.concat instead
`+` on strings — that's a type error waiting to happen (`"a" + "b"`)
tips: Mixing `..` with numbers is fine: `"Score: " .. score`
commonMistakes: Precedence surprises: `1 + 2 .. "!"` parses as `(1+2) .. "!"`, but `-x^2` is `-(x^2)`
Forgetting `%` on negatives: `-7 % 3` is `2` in Lua

examples.title: Operator tour
examples.code:
local seconds = 137
print(seconds // 60)          --> 2  (minutes)
print(seconds % 60)           --> 17 (leftover seconds)

local coins = 10
coins += 5                    --> 15
coins *= 2                    --> 30

local msg = "Coins: "
msg ..= tostring(coins)       --> "Coins: 30"
print(msg)

-- cycling through options
local modes = {"Easy", "Normal", "Hard"}
local slot = 1
slot = slot % #modes + 1      --> 2
slot = slot % #modes + 1      --> 3
slot = slot % #modes + 1      --> 1  (wraps around)
